# MapleSure Member Sign-In

MS MAPLESURE INSURANCE Group Benefits Digital Experience BUSINESS REQUIREMENT DOCUMENT · NEW APPLICATION Request ID REQ-2026-121 Raised by Group Benefits Digital Experience, MapleSure Insurance Business owner P. Moreau Domain Member Digital Access Type New application — no existing system provides this capability Priority High Requested date 2026-08-17

## Business objective

Give MapleSure members a standalone online sign-in — the front door for all future member-facing journeys — so that a member can authenticate themselves with their member ID and a password, and downstream portals can trust that authentication. MapleSure members currently have no dedicated online entry point: every digital journey begins with a phone call to the service desk for identity verification.

## Background and current state

There is no member-facing authentication capability today; portals under construction (claims, retirement) each assume "an authenticated member" and none provides authentication itself. The service desk performs manual identity verification by phone, which adds handling time to every member interaction and cannot scale to the online claim submission volumes forecast for next year. This is deliberately a new, separate application: authentication must be a shared front door, not a feature copied into each portal.

## Requirements


1. Sign-in page. A member can sign in with their member ID and password on a single, clearly branded MapleSure sign-in page.

2. Credential validation and landing view. Credentials are validated against the member credential store; a successful sign-in shows a signed-in landing view confirming the member's display name and last sign-in time.

3. Generic failure message. A failed sign-in shows one generic error message — it must not reveal whether the member ID or the password was wrong.

4. Temporary lockout. After five consecutive failed attempts for the same member ID, the account is temporarily locked for fifteen minutes and the page says so without revealing whether the credentials were otherwise correct.

5. Forgotten password link. A "Forgotten your password?" link is present and routes to a placeholder contact-the-service-desk page (self-serve reset is out of scope for this release).

6. Audit log. Every sign-in attempt (success, failure, lockout) is recorded in an audit log with member ID, timestamp and outcome — never the password.

7. Accessibility. The sign-in form is keyboard-accessible, labels every field, and meets WCAG AA contrast on the MapleSure palette.

8. Credential storage. Passwords are never stored or logged in plain text; the credential store holds salted hashes only.

## Out of scope

Self-serve password reset, multi-factor authentication, and federation with employer identity providers (future phases). Member registration/enrolment — credential records are provisioned by the existing membership back office.

## Success measures

A member with valid credentials reaches the signed-in landing view in one attempt. Invalid attempts never disclose which credential was wrong. Lockout engages on the fifth consecutive failure and releases after fifteen minutes. Zero passwords in any log or audit record.

## Notes for delivery

Keep the application small and self-contained: one sign-in page, one signed-in landing view, one placeholder help page, a credential store with salted hashes, and the audit log. Synthetic member data only.

## Sign-off
